title: Reducible partition step
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $F$ a set-valued etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $T$ a nonempty closed subset of $X$ that is not irreducible. Suppose every proper closed subset $Z\subsetneq T$ admits a finite lisse partition for the ambient sheaf $F$ [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-lisse-partition]. Then $T$ admits such a partition. No generic-lissity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The closed subspace T is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components. Enumerate them. Each component is closed in X and proper in T, since T is not irreducible. Choose its partition using the induction hypothesis.

For every part of component i, remove the inverse image of the union of earlier components. This is an open subscheme of that part. Compose its open immersion with the old immersion. The resulting images are the old images minus the earlier components, hence their finite union is T and they are pairwise disjoint.

Open pullback preserves local constancy. At a geometric point of the open, the inverse-image stalk bijection identifies the new stalk with the old finite stalk. The composition comparison identifies this iterated open restriction with the ambient pullback along the composite immersion. Thus the new parts form a finite lisse partition.

    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (T : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X) (hne : (T : Set X).Nonempty)

      Nonempty (EtaleLissePartition F (Z : Set X))) :
    Nonempty (EtaleLissePartition F (T : Set X))
